operations.description: Skip one upcoming run of a recurring schedule by `scheduleId`: the occurrence named by `occurrence` (milliseconds since the epoch), the next run or any after it, starts no workflow, and the runs around it fire as usual. Omitted, the next run is skipped, whichever it is. In a time zone the next wake-up can be the end of a daylight-saving gap that starts nothing, so the next run is the next real one; a run that is due but has not started is the next run. Skipped runs are listed as `skippedOccurrences` on the schedule until it moves past them, and `weft.schedules.unskip` takes one back. The skip leaves `revision` and `nextFireAt` as they are, and skipping a run already skipped changes nothing. A paused schedule accepts a skip of its runs counted from the first after now, and keeps it for when it is resumed. A fire moves neither `revision` nor `status`, so the run a caller read can start before the skip is written: the skip is refused with Conflict (reason `occurrence-not-next`) when `occurrence` is not an upcoming run as the write lands, whether a fire passed it or the cadence starts no run then. A schedule keeps at most 100 skipped runs, and one more is a Conflict. Pass `expectedRevision` to refuse the skip with StaleRevision when the schedule has changed since it was read; the revision is checked first. Faults with NotFound when no schedule with the given id exists, and with Conflict when the schedule is cancelled.

A run that has already passed cannot be taken back, and is refused with Conflict (reason `occurrence-not-next`). Pass `expectedRevision` to refuse it with StaleRevision when the schedule has changed since it was read; the revision is checked first. Faults with NotFound when no schedule with the given id exists, and with Conflict when the schedule is cancelled.

operations.description: Mark one deployment build removed, irreversibly. Only a draining build can be removed (drain it first with `weft.worker.deployments.drain`): a build that is not draining faults with Conflict (`reason: "version-not-draining"`). A build that does not exist, or was already removed, faults with NotFound. The current or ramping build of the routing pointer faults with Conflict (`reason: "version-routed"`). A build that durable work is still bound to faults with Conflict (`reason: "version-referenced"`): that work is every run that is not terminal (running, pending, or suspended) whose current worker binding names the build, under any worker-versioning policy, and every task-ledger entry that is not terminal whose execution requirement names the build; a dead-lettered entry is not terminal and keeps the build until it is cleared. Schedules and revision realms do not pin a build and do not count. A run, a task, or a retry that tries to bind to the build once it is removed fails with Conflict (`reason: "version-removed"`). If bindings keep landing on the build while the removal scans it, the removal gives up with Conflict (`reason: "version-busy"`); retry. A refused build is left as it was. A run keeps its newest 500 lines (the host sets the cap): `dropped` counts the older lines the cap evicted or retention removed. A line holds at most 2 KiB, its message and attributes together: a long message is cut and ends in a truncation marker, and attributes that do not fit beside it are dropped (`truncated` is true either way). Attributes are redacted before they are stored: any value under a key that names a secret outright (`card`, `cvv`, `ssn`, `pin`, `password`, `secret`, `apiKey`, ...) is `[REDACTED]`, as is a string, object or array under a looser key (`token`, `session`, `auth`) and any bearer token, JSON Web Token or card number, while a number or boolean under a loose key (`inputTokens: 12`) is kept. The message is not redacted. Lines are kept with the run; once the run has finished they are pruned after the host's retention window, and a run that is still active keeps its lines. operations.description: Start a workflow or deliver a signal to it if it already exists (signal-with-start). An absent target is created and delivered the signal in one batch; a non-terminal target (running, pending, or suspended) is signalled; a terminal target faults with Conflict unless `onTerminalConflict: "start-new"` is supplied with `id` and `signalId`, in which case the prior terminal run is replaced through the shared terminal-replacement path and the initial signal is delivered to the fresh run. A spent `idempotencyKey` whose run was purged or swept by retention also faults with Conflict. A signal name the target declares no signal for, when it declares its signals, faults with Unprocessable. Requires `type`, `signalName`, and exactly one of `signalId` or `idempotencyKey` (not both). Accepts `input`, `signalPayload`, and the non-idempotency start options from weft.workflows.start (`id`, `executionTimeout`, `startAt`/`startAfter`, `tags`, `searchAttributes`) plus `onTerminalConflict`; `idempotencyKey` is governed by the "exactly one of" rule above and cannot be combined with restart. Returns the workflow `id`. Concurrent callers converge on one workflow and one signal only with a shared `idempotencyKey`, or a shared `id` plus `signalId`; a bare `signalId` (no `id`/`idempotencyKey`) starts a fresh run per caller and does not converge.

executionTimeout.description: Total time the run may take before it times out: milliseconds, or a duration string such as "30s".

id.description: Client-chosen id of the target workflow. Omit it to have one generated. An absent id is created and signalled (outcome "started"); a non-terminal run with this id is signalled (outcome "signalled"); a finished run with this id faults with Conflict unless onTerminalConflict is "start-new".

idempotencyKey.description: Alternative to signalId; provide exactly one. Callers sharing a key converge on one run and one delivered signal (the signal id derives from the key), and a repeated key signals the run it first started instead of starting another. A key whose run was purged by retention faults with Conflict. Cannot be combined with signalId or with onTerminalConflict "start-new".

input.description: Input payload handed to the workflow body. Omit it for a workflow that takes no input.

onTerminalConflict.description: What to do when the supplied id belongs to a finished run: "error" (default) faults, "start-new" replaces it with a fresh run. "start-new" requires id and signalId and excludes idempotencyKey.

searchAttributes.description: Search attributes to index the run under, keyed by attribute name. Validated against the workflow type's declared schema; date-time values are ISO 8601 strings.

signalId.description: Id of the signal to deliver. Provide exactly one of signalId or idempotencyKey. Concurrent callers converge on one run and one signal only when they share both id and signalId; a bare signalId, without id, starts a fresh run per caller. Required for onTerminalConflict "start-new". At most 128 bytes.

operations.description: Invoke a named update handler on a workflow and wait for its result. Requires the workflow `id` and the update `name`; `payload` is optional. Unlike signals, updates return the handler result synchronously. Faults with NotFound when the workflow is not visible, InvalidParams when the payload exceeds the size limit, and Unprocessable when the workflow declares its updates and this name is not one of them. A Timeout fault carries the `updateId` in its `data`: the update stays queued, and its answer is read later with `weft.updates.result.get` or listed by `weft.workflows.updates.list`.

idempotencyKey.description: At-most-once key: a repeated key returns the first update's outcome instead of applying the update again.

payload.description: Payload passed to the update handler.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the update to be answered; defaults to 30000.

updateName.description: Name of the update handler to invoke.

workflowId.description: Id of the workflow to send the update to.

operations.name: weft.workflows.update
operations.summary: Send a synchronous update to a workflow

operations.description: Read a bounded page of the updates a workflow has received through the durable request path, newest first. Each entry has the update id, its name, when it was received, and its outcome (`pending`, `completed`, or `failed` with the failure message). A result is not listed: read it with `weft.updates.result.get` while it is kept. The history is kept until the workflow is purged. The cursor is opaque; a workflow that is unknown or purged lists no entries. An update is recorded when it is queued as a durable request: every update sent with `weft.workflows.update` (REST and JSON-RPC) and `engine.submitCoordinatedUpdate()`. It is not recorded when it is served without a request: the MCP `update_workflow` tool, and an in-process `engine.update()` or `handle.update()` answered by a live handler or a parked waiter, mint an id and write no entry.

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page, to read the next page; omit it for the first page.

limit.description: Maximum number of updates to return per page, 1 to 200; defaults to 50.

workflowId.description: Id of the workflow whose update history is listed.
